newsitem.title: HONG KONG: No Chinese New Year joy for HK stocks.
newsitem.headline: No Chinese New Year joy for HK stocks.

text.p: The festive mood of Chinese New Year is unlikely to spread into the Hong Kong stock market in the week ahead, with recent market weakness leaving investors feeling hesitant, analysts said.
The market will be closed on Thursday and Friday for the Lunar New Year. During the three-day week, the blue-chip Hang Seng Index looks set to remain around existing levels, analysts said.
"People are starting to be more cautious about the Hong Kong market," said Kelvin Tang, an analyst at ImPac Asset Management.
The Hang Seng Index rose 33.39 points, or 0.25 percent, to 13,321.79 last Friday. Over the week, the blue-chip index slipped 57.76 points, or 0.43 percent.

Analysts said concerns about the direction of interest rates continued to plague the market although the U.S. Federal Reserve was not expected to change its rate policy at the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on February 4 and 5.
"I think worries are definitely on the raising side rather than on the lowering side," said Julian Ings Chambers, assistant director at BZW Asia.
"The market has definitely been under pressure for the last week or so. It has run out of warrant steam, it has run out of good news and it is looking a little bit vulnerable short-term."

A recommendation by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority last Tuesday that banks limit mortgage lending for the purchase of luxury properties shook property stocks, and analysts said the sector remained fragile.
Ings Chambers said investors were worried about further measures to curb property speculation.
"It is not a question of what has been done but people worry about what might be done," he said.

Analysts said flows out of Hong Kong into other markets were also hurting prices. "Some funds are actually taking money out of Hong Kong and putting money in other regional markets," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities.
But Bank of East Asia Ltd's 1996 results are due on Monday and could prompt some buying interest in the banking sector, analysts said.
Net profit forecasts for the local commercial bank ranged from HK$1.79 billion to HK$1.95 billion compared with HK$1.64 billion posted for 1995.
"In general, we think there should be good results from Bank of East Asia, in fact all of the banks in 1996," Tsang said.
But ImPac's Tang said much of the good news had already been discounted. "Unless Bank of East Asia can indicate they did very well, their results will be neutral," he said.
Tang expected a trading range in the week ahead of 13,200 to 13,500 points. "People just don't know which direction the market is going," he said.
Ings Chambers said he would not be surprised to see a fall to 12,700 points.
"Next week should be pretty mixed. There is no reason to move significantly one way or the other but I would expect it to trend downwards," he said.
China Eastern Airlines Corp Ltd is set to become the first Chinese airline to list overseas this week, with a dual listing in Hong Kong and New York.

It offered 140 million H-shares in Hong Kong, representing 10 percent of a global offering of 1.4 billion shares, at HK$1.22 to HK$1.38 per share. The remaining 90 percent was divided equally into U.S. and international offerings.
Trading in the American Depositary Shares is expected to begin on Tuesday in New York and the H-shares are due to start trading on Wednesday in Hong Kong.

Consumer electronics products maker Chun Tai Holdings Ltd and Shui On Construction and Materials Ltd are due to make their stock market debuts on Monday. ($1 = HK$7.8) -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6345
